summary: Otto Maenchen-Helfen worked in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, and held posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (1927–1929), Mills College (1939–1947), and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Neugebauer was a historian and archaeologist who studied under Boris Turayev and at Graz, Munich, Copenhagen, and Göttingen. He held posts at Göttingen, Copenhagen, Brown University (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1945, 1950, 1969–1990).

Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Bonn under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, Sergey Oldenburg, Hermann Jacobi, and Rudolf Lange, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University (1911–1919).

Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University under doctoral supervisors Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He served at the Oriental Institute (1929) and at Charles University as Privatdozent (1922) and full professor (1930–1939).

Otto Strauß was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied in Berlin, Munich, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel University (1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Owen Flanagan is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Archbishop Stepinac High School, Fordham University, and Boston University. He was appointed Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.
Ozer Taye studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

P. A. Payutto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his bachelor's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1957–1962). He served as Associate Dean there (~1964–1974) and held a post at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

P. D. Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ceylon, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Eliot Deutsch and David J. Kalupahana, later serving as professor and Pali and Buddhist Studies department head at Ceylon (1997–2004).

P. K. Mukhopadhyay works in philosophy and Indology. He is a former professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University and is attested in 2009 as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research.
P. Pratap Kumar is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. In 2010, he is attested as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a visiting professor at Colorado College.
P. S. Chandrasekharan is an Indologist attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where he studied under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.
P. S. Sivaswami Iyer was an Indologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai (~1880–1884). In 1927, he served as President of the Editorial Board for the Journal of Oriental Research.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Bishop Heber College and the University of Madras. He held posts at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and served as Sanskrit department head at Annamalai University (1942–1947).
P. T. Narasimhachar was an Indologist who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under Mysore Hiriyanna around 1923–1926.

Padma Subrahmanyam is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University, completing research under supervisor Tiruvengadu Narayanayajwa Ramachandran (~1970–1979).

Padmanabh S. Jaini was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a professor and later professor emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley, with his career there attested between 1977 and 2016.

Palden Sherab was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche and Tubten Tsondru. He chaired the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).

Palmira Brummett is a historian, archaeologist, and Central Asian scholar who studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She held posts at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and Brown University (2011–2016).
